chunks.title: Photoreceptors, RPE & imaging
chunks.tldr: Cones packed at the fovea (1:1 cone→ganglion cell; acuity, colour, photopic). Rods in periphery (night, motion; many rods per ganglion cell). Rhodopsin = scotopsin + 11-cis retinal (vit A); light → all-trans; peak ~500 nm. Cones peak 430 (blue), 540 (green), 575 (red). RPE: eats outer segments, recycles vitamin A, absorbs scatter, outer blood-retinal barrier; inner layer of Bruch's; barely regenerates. Imaging: photos, FFA, OCT, ICGA, FAF, OCT-A, wide-field.
points: Dark-adapted sensitivity shifts from 500 nm (rods) to ~560 nm (cones) in light (Purkinje shift).
chunks.hook: Cones for Colour & Centre; Rods for Rim & dim.

cards.a: About 500 nm (blue-green).

chunks.title: AMD: risk, staging & dry disease
chunks.tldr: Leading cause of irreversible blindness in the elderly (developed world). Risk: age, white, female, smoking, genes CFH (1q) and ARMS2/HTRA1 (10q). Beckman staging: small drusen <63 µm = normal ageing; medium 63–125 µm = early; large >125 µm or pigment change = intermediate; late = neovascular and/or geographic atrophy. Reticular pseudodrusen (subretinal drusenoid deposits; best on infrared/FAF) = high-risk. GA: sharp RPE/photoreceptor loss with visible choroidal vessels; monitor with FAF (dark).
points: AREDS for intermediate AMD or late AMD in one eye: vit C 500 mg, vit E 400 IU, zinc 80 mg, copper 2 mg (+ lutein/zeaxanthin instead of β-carotene in smokers).
chunks.hook: Big drusen (>125 µm, a vein's width at the disc) = intermediate AMD → AREDS.

cards.a: Complement factor H (CFH, 1q31) and ARMS2/HTRA1 (10q26).

cards.q: Why avoid beta-carotene in smokers taking AREDS?
cards.a: Increased lung cancer risk.

chunks.title: Neovascular AMD & anti-VEGF
chunks.tldr: CNV through Bruch's: type 1 (occult, sub-RPE, fibrovascular PED), type 2 (classic, subretinal; lacy early leak on FFA), type 3 = RAP (retinal angiomatous proliferation; intraretinal haemorrhage, retinochoroidal anastomosis). Symptoms: sudden distortion/central blur. OCT shows intra/subretinal fluid; FFA most sensitive for CNV. Rx: intravitreal anti-VEGF — bevacizumab (off-label, full antibody), ranibizumab (Fab), aflibercept (VEGFR1/2 trap, also PlGF, longer-acting, 8-weekly non-inferior). Load 3 monthly → treat-and-extend/PRN.
points: Bevacizumab = ranibizumab in efficacy and safety (CATT/IVAN).
Anti-VEGF beats laser, PDT and surgery.
chunks.hook: Sudden wavy lines in an older person = wet AMD → inject within 2 weeks.

cards.a: Early well-defined lacy hyperfluorescence with late leakage.

cards.q: What does aflibercept bind besides VEGF-A?
cards.a: VEGF-B and placental growth factor (PlGF).

chunks.title: Myopic macular degeneration
chunks.tldr: Pathological myopia (>6 D, long axial length; common in East Asia). Signs: peripapillary atrophy, tilted disc, posterior staphyloma, lacquer cracks (Bruch's breaks; can bleed without CNV), Förster-Fuchs spot (pigmented scar of CNV). Myopic CNV in 5–10% → anti-VEGF (few injections needed). Also myopic foveoschisis (surgery if progressing), macular hole RD, peripheral lattice/RD.
chunks.hook: Long eye → stretched Bruch's → cracks, holes and new vessels.

cards.a: A raised pigmented macular lesion in pathological myopia from regressed CNV with RPE proliferation.

chunks.title: DR: pathology, screening & grading
chunks.tldr: Hyperglycaemia → pericyte loss, BM thickening → microaneurysms, leakage, capillary closure → ischaemia → VEGF. Screen: type 1 within 3–5 y of diagnosis, type 2 at diagnosis, then yearly; pregnancy each trimester. Grades: mild NPDR (MAs only), moderate, severe NPDR = 4-2-1 rule (haemorrhages in 4 quadrants, venous beading in 2, IRMA in 1). PDR: NVD/NVE; high-risk = NVD >⅓ DD, any NVD + VH, NVE >½ DD + VH. CSME (ETDRS): thickening within 500 µm of centre, exudate within 500 µm with thickening, or ≥1 DA thickening within 1 DD; now OCT 'centre-involving'.
points: Flame haem = superficial NFL (arteriolar); dot-blot = deep; CWS = NFL infarct.
Type 1 → more PDR; type 2 → more macular oedema.
Wide-field imaging finds peripheral lesions that predict progression.
chunks.hook: 4-2-1: haems in 4, beading in 2, IRMA in 1 = severe NPDR.

cards.a: Severe NPDR: intraretinal haemorrhages in 4 quadrants, venous beading in 2, or IRMA in 1.
NVD ≥⅓ disc area, any NVD with VH, or NVE ≥½ disc area with VH.

chunks.title: Treating diabetic retinopathy
chunks.tldr: Control glucose, BP, lipids. Centre-involving DMO: anti-VEGF (load 3–6 monthly, then PRN/treat-and-extend) — gains maintained >5 y; laser for non-centre CSME or as adjunct. PDR: PRP (thousands of burns outside the arcades) halves severe visual loss; anti-VEGF alternative/adjunct. Severe NPDR: PRP if poor follow-up/control (esp. type 2). Vitrectomy: non-clearing VH, tractional RD threatening the macula, combined TRD/RRD; pre-op anti-VEGF ~2 wk reduces bleeding.
points: Ischaemic maculopathy (enlarged FAZ) = poor prognosis, doesn't respond well.
chunks.hook: New vessels → laser the periphery; swollen centre → inject.

cards.a: Non-clearing vitreous haemorrhage, macula-threatening tractional RD, combined tractional-rhegmatogenous RD.

chunks.title: Retinal vein occlusion
chunks.tldr: Sudden painless blur, >50 y; risks HTN, diabetes, lipids, glaucoma/raised IOP, hyperviscosity. CRVO: haemorrhages in all 4 quadrants ('blood and thunder'), tortuous veins, disc swelling. BRVO: sector at an AV crossing (usually superotemporal). Macular oedema → anti-VEGF (ranibizumab/aflibercept) or dexamethasone implant (Ozurdex); grid laser helps BRVO not CRVO. Ischaemic CRVO (~⅓; VA <6/60, RAPD, >10 DA non-perfusion) → half get NVI/NVA → neovascular glaucoma ('90-day glaucoma') → PRP ± anti-VEGF. BRVO with >5 DA ischaemia → NVE in 40% → sector PRP.
chunks.hook: Ischaemic CRVO: watch the iris for 3 months (100-day glaucoma).

cards.a: VA worse than 6/60, RAPD, >10 disc areas of capillary non-perfusion on FFA, many CWS/haemorrhages.

cards.q: Why check IOP in vein occlusion?
cards.a: Glaucoma/ocular hypertension is a risk factor (and NVG a complication).

chunks.title: Retinal artery occlusion & macroaneurysm
chunks.tldr: CRAO: sudden profound painless loss (CF–LP in 90%), RAPD at once, pale swollen retina with cherry-red spot, box-carring; ~25% have a cilioretinal artery sparing the centre. Fades in 4–6 wk to pale disc. Emergency: exclude GCA (ESR/CRP, steroids) and treat as stroke (carotid Doppler, echo, risk factors). Attempts: ocular massage, paracentesis, IOP-lowering, vasodilators, thrombolysis — little proven. BRAO: field defect, often embolic (Hollenhorst). Macroaneurysm: elderly hypertensive women, superotemporal arteriole, 'hourglass' multilevel haemorrhage; usually self-thromboses; laser if exudate threatens fovea.
points: OCT: acute inner retinal hyperreflective thickening → later inner retinal thinning.
chunks.hook: Old patient + CRAO = ask about jaw claudication before anything else.

cards.q: Why does CRAO cause a cherry-red spot?
cards.a: The thin foveola lets the normal choroid show through, surrounded by opaque infarcted inner retina.

cards.q: Classic haemorrhage pattern of retinal arterial macroaneurysm?
cards.a: Multilevel ('hourglass') — sub-ILM/preretinal, intraretinal and subretinal at once.

chunks.title: Rhegmatogenous RD
chunks.tldr: Break + traction + liquid vitreous. Horseshoe tear (PVD traction; superotemporal), round hole (lattice), dialysis (blunt trauma, inferotemporal, young). Risks: myopia, lattice, cataract surgery, trauma, fellow-eye RD. Symptoms: flashes, floaters, curtain. Surgery: pneumatic retinopexy (single small superior break, no PVR), scleral buckle (92–94%; young phakic, dialysis), vitrectomy (superior/posterior/multiple breaks, VH, PVR, pseudophakic) with gas/oil. Macula-on = urgent; macula-off: delay ≤1 week doesn't worsen outcome.
points: Buckle complications: refractive change (myopic shift), diplopia, extrusion.
Vitrectomy with gas/oil accelerates cataract; posturing needed.
chunks.hook: Macula on? Operate today. Macula off? Within the week.

cards.q: Where are retinal dialyses typically found?
cards.a: Inferotemporally (often after blunt trauma in young patients).
Single (or close) small break in the superior two-thirds, minimal SRF, no PVR or significant traction.

chunks.title: Tractional & exudative RD, peripheral degenerations
chunks.tldr: Tractional: PDR, PVR, ROP, trauma; concave, immobile, doesn't reach ora; vitrectomy + membrane removal. Exudative: no break, shifting fluid, smooth convex; VKH, posterior scleritis, tumours, CSCR, Coats → treat cause. Lattice: 6–10% of people, myopes, white lines + pigment, firm adhesion at margins; found in 20–30% of RDs but rarely needs prophylaxis. Retinoschisis vs RD: schisis = absolute scotoma, smooth dome, no pigment cells, no demarcation line, laser 'whitens'; RD = relative scotoma, corrugated, tobacco dust, demarcation line if chronic. Paving-stone, white-without-pressure = benign.
points: Reticular schisis with inner + outer holes → full-thickness RD → treat.
chunks.hook: Tobacco dust in the vitreous = there's a break somewhere.

cards.q: Visual field difference between retinoschisis and RD?
cards.a: Schisis gives an absolute scotoma; RD gives a relative scotoma.

chunks.title: Macular hole, ERM & traumatic maculopathy
chunks.tldr: Macular hole: elderly women, idiopathic tangential vitreous traction; central scotoma, Watzke-Allen broken beam. Gass stages 1 (impending yellow spot) → 2 (<400 µm FT) → 3 (>400 µm) → 4 (with PVD). Rx: vitrectomy + ILM peel (dyes) + gas, face-down; ≥90% close. ERM: cellophane sheen, striae, pseudohole; peel if distortion. Trauma: commotio retinae (Berlin oedema), choroidal rupture (crescent concentric to disc → late CNV), Purtscher (crush/pancreatitis; white patches + haemorrhages), Terson (SAH → VH), solar retinopathy.

cards.a: Intraocular (vitreous/preretinal) haemorrhage associated with subarachnoid haemorrhage/raised ICP.
Choroidal neovascularisation.

chunks.title: CSCR, CME & angioid streaks
chunks.tldr: CSCR: young/middle-aged men, type A, stress, steroids (any route); serous macular detachment, micropsia, hyperopic shift. FFA: smokestack or ink-blot leak; ICG choroidal hyperpermeability. 80% resolve in 6 months; chronic → half-dose PDT, micropulse, laser if extrafoveal leak. CME: petaloid FFA, honeycomb OCT; causes uveitis, DR, RVO, ERM, drugs, RP; Irvine-Gass after cataract (peaks 4–12 wk) → topical NSAID + steroid, then periocular/intravitreal triamcinolone. Angioid streaks: Bruch's cracks radiating from disc — PXE (ABCC6), Paget, Ehlers-Danlos, sickle ('PEPSi'); CNV → anti-VEGF; avoid trauma (choroidal rupture).
chunks.hook: Stressed young man + steroids + blister at macula = CSCR — stop the steroid.

cards.a: Smokestack (or ink-blot) leak into a serous detachment.
Pseudoxanthoma elasticum, Paget disease, Ehlers-Danlos, sickle cell/haemoglobinopathies.

chunks.title: White dot syndromes
chunks.tldr: POHS: histo spots + peripapillary scarring, no vitritis, CNV → anti-VEGF. APMPPE: young adults post-viral, bilateral grey placoid lesions; FFA early block, late stain; recovers; may have CNS vasculitis. Serpiginous: older men, peripapillary snake-like spreading atrophy, recurrent contiguous; exclude TB; immunosuppress. Birdshot: HLA-A29, cream ovoid spots, vasculitis, CME; ERG to monitor; needs steroid-sparing therapy. MEWDS: young women, unilateral, transient dots, enlarged blind spot, self-limits. AMN: wedge-shaped red-brown parafoveal lesions, persisting scotomas. AZOOR: field loss with little to see.
chunks.hook: Birdshot = A29; Serpiginous snakes from the disc; MEWDS melts away.

cards.a: HLA-A29.
Early hypofluorescence (blockage) with late hyperfluorescence (staining).

chunks.title: Macular dystrophies
chunks.tldr: X-linked retinoschisis (RS1, Müller cells): boys, spoke-wheel foveal schisis, peripheral schisis 50%; FFA no leak (≠ CME); negative ERG (b < a). Cone/cone-rod dystrophy: photophobia, poor colour, falling VA; bull's-eye; ERG cones lost (exclude chloroquine). Stargardt (ABCA4, AR): commonest; childhood VA loss with little to see early → beaten-bronze macula + pisciform flecks; dark choroid on FFA, FAF crucial; avoid vitamin A supplements. Best (BEST1, AD): egg-yolk vitelliform lesion → pseudohypopyon → vitelliruptive; abnormal EOG, normal ERG.
points: Enhanced S-cone (Goldmann-Favre): AR, foveal schisis + nummular pigment at arcades.
chunks.hook: Best disease: Bad EOG, Everything else fine.

cards.a: Abnormal EOG (reduced Arden ratio) with normal ERG.
Negative waveform — reduced b-wave with relatively preserved a-wave.

chunks.title: Retinitis pigmentosa & other degenerations
chunks.tldr: RP (1 in 5000): nyctalopia + ring scotoma → tunnel vision. Triad: bone-spicules, attenuated arterioles, waxy disc pallor; ERG reduced/absent (rods first). Inheritance: X-linked worst, AR severe, AD best. Complications: PSC cataract, CME (CAIs), ERM, glaucoma, keratoconus, Coats-like. Syndromic: Usher (deaf), Bardet-Biedl, Refsum, Kearns-Sayre. Avoid smoking, HCQ, phenothiazines, vigabatrin. LCA: blind infant, nystagmus, flat ERG; RPE65 gene therapy (voretigene). Gyrate atrophy: ↑ornithine (OAT), scalloped atrophy; low-arginine diet, B6. Fundus albipunctatus: stationary night blindness, white dots, slow dark adaptation.
chunks.hook: Can't see at night + bony spicules + thin arteries + waxy disc = RP.

cards.a: Posterior subcapsular cataract.

cards.q: Biochemical defect and diet in gyrate atrophy?
cards.a: Ornithine aminotransferase deficiency → hyperornithinaemia; arginine-restricted diet ± pyridoxine.

chunks.title: Colour vision defects
chunks.tldr: Red and green opsin genes on X; blue on chromosome 7. Red-green dichromacy (protan = red, deutan = green): X-linked, 8% of men, 0.5% of women, normal acuity. Tritan (blue-yellow): AD, rare — and the typical acquired pattern of retinal/macular disease. Blue cone monochromacy: X-linked, rare. Rod monochromacy (achromatopsia): AR, no cones → low VA, photophobia, nystagmus. Acquired defects: asymmetric, affect both sexes equally.
chunks.hook: Congenital = red-green, both eyes, men. Acquired = often blue-yellow, one eye worse.

cards.q: Prevalence of congenital red-green colour deficiency?
cards.a: About 8% of males and 0.5% of females (X-linked recessive).

chunks.title: Benign retinal tumours & CHRPE
chunks.tldr: Astrocytoma (astrocytic hamartoma): white 'mulberry' NFL nodule; multiple/bilateral → tuberous sclerosis. Capillary haemangioma (von Hippel): red ball with dilated feeder artery & draining vein, exudate/RD; VHL gene chr 3p → screen for cerebellar haemangioblastoma, RCC, phaeo; laser/cryo small lesions. Combined hamartoma: grey, gliotic, tortuous vessels near disc → NF2. CHRPE: flat black lesion with lacunae (unifocal); 'bear tracks' (grouped, benign); multiple bilateral pisciform lesions → Gardner/FAP → colonoscopy.
points: Retinoma: arrested retinoblastoma (calcified, translucent) — monitor for life; relatives may carry RB1.
Medulloepithelioma: child's ciliary body cystic mass ± lens coloboma, NVG.
chunks.hook: Scattered bilateral fish-tail CHRPEs = check the colon (FAP).

cards.q: Retinal capillary haemangioma is linked to which gene/syndrome?
cards.a: VHL tumour suppressor gene (3p25) — von Hippel-Lindau disease.

cards.q: Which CHRPE pattern indicates familial adenomatous polyposis?
cards.a: Multiple, bilateral, scattered pigmented lesions (often pisciform with depigmented tails).

chunks.title: Retinoblastoma
chunks.tldr: Commonest primary intraocular malignancy of childhood (~1 in 15–18,000). RB1 tumour suppressor, 13q14 (two hits). Bilateral/multifocal = germline → AD, ~90% penetrance, 50% risk to offspring; most unilateral = sporadic. Presents with leukocoria (median 12 mo bilateral, 24 mo unilateral), strabismus, red eye/NVG, pseudohypopyon. White calcified mass (US/CT calcium), endophytic/exophytic, vitreous seeds. MRI brain/orbits (trilateral RB = pineoblastoma). Rx: laser/cryo (small), plaque, IV or intra-arterial chemo + focal; intravitreal melphalan for seeds; EBRT reserved; enucleation for advanced — histology for optic nerve/choroid invasion.
points: Unaffected parents of one affected child: 4–7% risk for the next child.
Germline carriers: lifelong second cancer risk (osteosarcoma), worse after radiotherapy.
chunks.hook: White pupil in a photo = retinoblastoma until proven otherwise.

cards.a: RB1 tumour suppressor gene on 13q14.
Bilateral retinoblastoma plus a pineoblastoma (or other midline intracranial PNET).

chunks.title: Primary vitreoretinal lymphoma & retinal metastasis
chunks.tldr: PVRL: older adults, bilateral 80%, vitreous cells (sheets) + yellow sub-RPE infiltrates, poor steroid response — the classic masquerade. Usually diffuse large B-cell; linked to primary CNS lymphoma → brain MRI, LP. Diagnosis: diagnostic vitrectomy (cytology, flow, IL-10:IL-6 >1, MYD88). Rx: intravitreal methotrexate, EBRT, systemic high-dose MTX. Retinal metastasis: rare (unlike choroid), pale infiltrates; = brain metastasis prognosis.
chunks.hook: Elderly 'uveitis' that won't respond to steroids = lymphoma — biopsy the vitreous.

cards.a: Intravitreal methotrexate (± ocular radiotherapy), with systemic/CNS therapy as needed.
